summary.text: 系 (xì) is associated with thread, binding, and connection, and is also used for lineage and system. One paleographic interpretation sees an early hand holding connected silk; the received Shuowen analysis instead treats 糸 as semantic and 丿 as phonetic. The accounts remain unresolved.

formation.text: Disputed. Oracle-bone and bronze forms are interpreted as a hand holding connected silk, conveying binding or connection. In a separate received analysis, 系 consists of 糸, associated with thread, and 丿 as a sound element. Another proposal identifies 系 as an early form of 攣; the evidence here does not settle these analyses. The curated seal-script image is a modern redraw, not a dated artifact or proof of sequence.

components.text: The visible upper stroke is 丿. In the received Shuowen analysis, it supplies sound; a paleographic account instead interprets seal-script 丿 as a reduced 爪, part of a hand holding silk. The proposed hand reading is disputed, and neither analysis is conclusively established here.

sound_limitation.text: The sound role is part of the received Shuowen analysis, but the competing paleographic account treats this shape as a reduced hand. The supplied evidence does not independently resolve the component’s identity or establish its historical reading.

components.text: 糸 is visible in the received analysis and is associated with thread. In the alternative hand-and-silk account, it represents the silk held in the depicted scene; the whole graph is interpreted as binding or connection.

history.text: Oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as a hand holding connected silk. The alternative account that 系 is an early form of 攣 and the received Shuowen parsing remain unresolved; the seal-script form supplied here is a modern redraw, not an independently dated artifact image.

系 is explicitly analyzed as a sound element in 係, whose separate graph is described as 人 with 糸 and associated with binding a person with a cord. Related records also connect 系 with 係 and 繫, but the dossier does not establish a single graphic chronology or prove that 系 is a regular simplification of 繫.

Reported early uses include ritual and place or state names, and a later bronze personal name; these are not dated milestones for the meanings of thread, connection, lineage, or system. A Warring States use of 系 to write 奚 is also reported, but the sound match and old name underlying such a use are not established here.

uncertainties.text: The earliest inscriptional forms and their dates are not independently established in this dossier. It reports competing accounts of the graph’s structure, including the reduced-hand interpretation, the Shuowen sound-element analysis, and a proposal linking 系 to 攣.
The evidence proposes a development from connection to lineage, with a Han-dynasty textual example, but does not document intermediate stages or a historical path to the modern gloss “system.”

The supplied Baxter–Sagart rows give 系 MC hejH and OC *[m]-kˤek-s, and 係 MC kejH and OC *kˤek-s. Sources attest 系 as a phonetic element in 係, but these distinct reconstructed forms do not resolve the precise historical sound relation. The exact rows were supplied locally rather than verified in the opened online table.

senses.text: A thread gloss is recorded, and the hand-and-connected-silk interpretation associates the graph with silk and binding. The dossier does not identify this as the earliest attested lexical use or establish the dates of the relevant inscriptions.
Binding or connection is the proposed meaning of the hand holding connected silk. This is an interpretation of the graphic origin, not a securely dated earliest use.

senses.period: historical; cited in a Han-dynasty text
senses.text: A source proposes that the connection sense extended to lineage and cites a Han-dynasty example. The intermediate history is not documented here.
System is a recorded modern gloss, but the dossier gives no evidence for when or how this meaning developed.

senses.gloss: use of 系 to write 奚
senses.text: A reported Warring States use writes 奚 with 系. This is a graph used for another word, not evidence that the meaning of 系 developed into the word-level meaning of 奚; the old word’s sound comparison is not supplied.

developments.text: A source proposes an extension from connection to lineage and gives a Han-dynasty textual example, but the intervening stages are not documented.

limitations.text: The reported ritual, place/state, and personal-name uses are not independently dated here as attestations of the listed lexical senses.
The modern gloss system has no supported chronology or semantic development in this dossier.

overview.text: 系 (xì) is used for thread, connection, lineage, and system. Its proposed picture of a hand holding connected silk suggests binding, but that origin is disputed against an older analysis of 糸 plus a sound element.

components.text: This upper stroke is read as a sound element in one account; another sees it as part of the hand in a silk-binding picture. The evidence does not settle the difference.
糸 is associated with thread or silk, which appears in both the received parsing and the alternative picture of silk held by a hand.

relationships.text: 系 is explicitly treated as a sound element in 係. Both have modern Mandarin xì; supplied Baxter–Sagart rows give 系 MC hejH, OC *[m]-kˤek-s and 係 MC kejH, OC *kˤek-s. The source-attested role is clear, but the distinct reconstructed forms and locally supplied rows do not establish the precise historical sound development.

The dossier records related or interchangeable use of 系 and 係, but does not establish when or how broadly they functioned as graphic variants. This character-level relation does not make 人 a component of 系.

Records list 系 as a counterpart or variant of 繫, while another account proposes simplification from 繫. The supplied evidence does not establish a graphic chronology or a regular simplification relation.
